html:
A railway across the Isthmus of Panama, from the Atlantic side to Panama City on the Pacific, built from 1850 to 1855. About 76 kilometres long, it was the first railway to cross the Americas from ocean to ocean.

An American company built it, then on land belonging to New Granada (Colombia). The California Gold Rush made it urgent: thousands of people were crossing the isthmus on foot and by canoe to reach the ships for San Francisco. Work went through swamp and jungle, in heavy rain. Thousands of workers, from Ireland, China, the Caribbean, Europe and the Americas, died of yellow fever, cholera and malaria. The exact toll is unknown.

When it opened in 1855, the railway cut the crossing from days to a few hours, and it was hugely profitable. Its business fell when the first US transcontinental railroad opened in 1869. Its route guided the later Panama Canal, and the railway still runs beside it.
sum: A railway across the Isthmus of Panama, from the Atlantic side to Panama City on the Pacific, built from 1850 to 1855. About 76 kilometres long, it was the first railway to cross the Americas from ocean to ocean.
